project.title: Agentic AI Supply Chain Disruption Monitoring System
project.goal: Build a complete production-style AI-powered supply chain disruption monitoring and mitigation system. The system must detect disruptions, analyze their impact, recommend mitigation actions, require human approval, and use Hindsight as the long-term memory of previous disruption events, decisions, and outcomes.
project.important_instruction: Build the complete working application, not a mockup or static prototype. Use real application logic, persistent storage, working APIs, working agent workflows, and a functional frontend. Do not invent metrics, reviews, statistics, customer numbers, or performance claims. If data is simulated, clearly label it as simulated.

frontend.requirements: Build a professional supply-chain operations dashboard. Include: - Dashboard - Disruption monitoring - Disruption details - Impact analysis - Mitigation recommendations - Approval workflow - Supplier information - Inventory information - Purchase orders - Analytics - Historical memory - Agent reasoning/explainability - Simulator

backend.responsibilities: - REST API - Database operations - Supply-chain monitoring - Disruption processing - Agent orchestration - Hindsight integration - Human approval workflow - Alert generation - Historical experience retrieval

agents.agent: Monitor supplier, inventory, logistics, and external conditions.
Detect abnormal events and determine whether they represent meaningful supply-chain disruptions.
Calculate inventory coverage, demand pressure, stockout risk, and expected supply gaps.
Determine the operational impact of the disruption, including inventory risk, delivery risk, and business impact.
Evaluate possible suppliers and mitigation strategies. This agent must use Hindsight recall to retrieve relevant previous disruption experiences and successful or unsuccessful mitigation decisions.
Generate actionable alerts and prepare a response plan.
Review the proposed decision, evidence, confidence, and historical context before presenting the recommendation for human approval.

database.purpose: PostgreSQL is the operational database for the current state of the supply chain.

entities.entity: Store supplier information, capabilities, lead time, reliability, location, and status.
Store current inventory quantity, demand rate, safety stock, reorder information, and related supplier information.
Store purchase orders, quantities, expected delivery dates, supplier information, and status.
Store currently active and resolved disruption cases.
Store generated alerts and their status.
Store recommendations waiting for human approval and their approval/rejection status.

database.important: Do not use PostgreSQL as the long-term AI memory system. PostgreSQL stores current operational truth. Hindsight stores long-term experiential memory.

hindsight.purpose: Hindsight is the long-term memory layer for the AI agents. It must store previous disruption experiences, agent decisions, mitigation actions, and outcomes so future decisions can use historical experience.

deployment.network: Hindsight runs locally on the same laptop as the project.

workflow.step: When a disruption is resolved, retain the important experience in Hindsight.
When a new disruption is detected, retrieve relevant historical experiences using recall.
Pass recalled experiences to the Alternative Supplier and Mitigation Agent.
Use the historical information together with current SQL data to produce the recommendation.

hindsight.important: Use Hindsight as the long-term memory system. Do not create another database specifically for long-term agent memory.
hindsight.llm: Do not introduce a separate LLM solely for explanations unless it is actually required by the selected Hindsight configuration. The current project does not require a dedicated LLM explanation layer.

system_flow.step: Collect current supplier, inventory, logistics, weather, and operational information.
Store current operational information in PostgreSQL.
Supply Chain Monitoring Agent continuously checks the current state.
Disruption Detection Agent identifies abnormal or disruptive events.
Inventory and Demand Analysis Agent calculates stock coverage and potential shortages.
Impact Assessment Agent determines the severity and business impact.
Alternative Supplier and Mitigation Agent calls Hindsight recall to retrieve similar historical experiences.
The mitigation agent combines: current SQL data + current disruption information + recalled Hindsight experiences.
Reviewer Agent checks the recommendation and supporting evidence.
Alert and Response Planning Agent generates an actionable alert.
Human reviews and approves or rejects the recommendation.
Execute only approved actions. Never automatically switch suppliers or place purchases without explicit human approval.
After the disruption is resolved, retain the disruption, decision, action, approval, and outcome in Hindsight.

example.scenario: Supplier ABC reports a 10-day delivery delay.
example.current_data: Inventory = 25 tonnes. Daily demand = 5 tonnes. Current inventory coverage = 5 days. Delayed shipment arrives after the expected stockout.
example.hindsight: Search previous experiences involving Supplier ABC and similar steel delivery disruptions.
example.decision: Identify suitable alternative suppliers and mitigation strategies. Consider both current supplier information and historical outcomes.
example.approval: Present the recommendation to the human operator.
example.outcome: After resolution, store the actual outcome as a new Hindsight memory.

learning_demo.objective: Clearly demonstrate that the system improves its recommendations through historical experience.
learning_demo.first_event: Introduce a disruption for Supplier ABC. The system has no relevant previous experience. Generate a recommendation and store the final outcome.
learning_demo.second_event: Trigger another similar disruption involving Supplier ABC. Hindsight should retrieve the previous experience.
learning_demo.visible_result: Show the operator: - Previous disruption - Previous recommendation - Previous outcome - Retrieved memory - Current disruption - Updated recommendation

api.endpoint: Create a controlled disruption for demonstration and testing.
Return relevant Hindsight memories associated with the disruption.
Return the explainability information for the current case.

ui.design: Professional enterprise supply-chain operations interface. Clean, modern, technical, readable, and suitable for a hackathon demonstration.
ui.navigation: Use a clean sidebar or top navigation. Keep navigation simple and consistent.
ui.dashboard: Display actual values retrieved from the backend. Show active disruptions, inventory risks, pending approvals, affected suppliers, and recent events.
ui.disruption_page: Show: - Event information - Supplier - Delay - Inventory coverage - Impact - Risk factors - Recommended mitigation - Historical Hindsight memories - Agent reasoning/evidence - Human approval controls
ui.memory_page: Show relevant historical experiences retrieved from Hindsight. Make it obvious why each memory is relevant to the current case.
ui.simulation_page: Allow judges to trigger predefined disruption scenarios. Provide scenarios such as: - Supplier delay - Logistics disruption - Inventory shortage - Weather-related disruption

design_restrictions.restriction: Do NOT use pill-shaped buttons. Use normal rectangular buttons with modest border radius.
Do NOT create fake reviews or testimonials.
Do NOT create fake metrics or fabricated performance statistics. Every displayed metric must come from actual system data or be explicitly marked as simulated/demo data.
Do NOT use emoji icons. Use a consistent professional icon library if icons are required.
Do NOT use crazy scroll animations. Avoid excessive animations and unnecessary motion.
Do NOT use em dashes anywhere in UI text, documentation, comments, or generated content.
Do NOT make the interface look like a marketing landing page. It should look like a real operational AI system.
Do NOT use fake customer logos, fake company names, fake testimonials, fake awards, or fabricated statistics.

data.requirement: Provide realistic simulated supply-chain data for development and demonstration.
Clearly mark simulated data inside the UI where appropriate.
Create enough suppliers, inventory items, purchase orders, and disruption scenarios to demonstrate the complete workflow.
Do not present simulated data as real-world data.

security.requirements: - Store secrets in environment variables. - Never hardcode API keys. - Validate all API inputs. - Implement basic authentication/authorization structure where appropriate. - Do not expose database credentials to the frontend. - Do not expose internal Hindsight configuration to the frontend.

services.service: Self-hosted Hindsight service for long-term agent memory.

docker.requirement: Create a docker-compose.yml that starts all required services.
Configure service-to-service networking through Docker Compose.

project_structure.structure: frontend/ backend/ agents/ api/ database/ models/ services/ hindsight/ workflows/ utils/ tests/ docker/ scripts/ docker-compose.yml .env.example README.md

testing.requirements: Write tests for: - Database operations - Inventory calculations - Disruption detection - Impact assessment - Supplier comparison - Hindsight retain - Hindsight recall - Agent workflow - Approval workflow - API endpoints
testing.requirement: Include an end-to-end test that simulates a disruption, generates a recommendation, approves it, records the outcome, and verifies that the experience is retained in Hindsight.

explainability.requirement: Every recommendation must show the evidence and reasoning used by the agents.
Clearly distinguish: - Current SQL data - Retrieved Hindsight memories - Agent conclusions - Human decision
The UI must make the Hindsight contribution visible.

development.requirement: Start by inspecting the complete existing project if source code is provided. Preserve useful existing functionality instead of unnecessarily rewriting it.
Integrate Hindsight into the existing architecture rather than rebuilding the entire system around Hindsight.
Do not create redundant long-term memory tables when Hindsight is being used for that purpose.
Keep Hindsight for long-term experiential memory.
Keep human approval before consequential supply-chain actions.
Make every feature functional before adding visual polish.
After implementation, run the backend tests, frontend build, Docker Compose startup, database migrations, and end-to-end disruption simulation.
Fix all errors encountered during testing.

demo.sequence: 1. Supplier ABC experiences a delivery delay. 2. Monitoring detects the disruption. 3. Inventory agent calculates the remaining stock coverage. 4. Impact agent determines the expected shortage. 5. Mitigation agent searches Hindsight. 6. Relevant historical experience is displayed. 7. Alternative suppliers are evaluated. 8. Recommendation is generated. 9. Reviewer checks the recommendation. 10. Human approves the recommendation. 11. Disruption is resolved. 12. Final outcome is retained in Hindsight. 13. Trigger a similar disruption again. 14. Hindsight recalls the previous experience. 15. The system demonstrates how historical experience influences the new recommendation.
demo.objective: The final demonstration must clearly prove that Hindsight provides persistent long-term memory and that the AI system can use previous operational experiences to improve future decision-making.
